boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: No-admission activities and campus programs with direct evidence of free access.

cards.title: See the Simons Center Gallery
cards.subtitle: Simons Center for Geometry and Physics
cards.notes: Meet up during weekday gallery hours to view the current exhibition, then use the lobby to compare favorite pieces and ideas.
cards.short_summary: A free, public art-and-science gallery stop on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Simons Center Gallery exhibitions and special events are free and open to the public; gallery hours are Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public. Gallery hours listed as Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; closed weekends and holidays.

cards.title: Join a Zuccaire Gallery program
cards.subtitle: Staller Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Plan a gallery visit around an artist talk, tour, or outreach program, and leave time to discuss the work together afterward.
cards.short_summary: Free public gallery programming inside the Staller Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Paul W. Zuccaire Gallery states that all of its events, outreach, and education programs are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of the Staller Center; gallery programs are free and open to the public.

cards.title: Explore CommUniversity Day
cards.subtitle: Stony Brook University campus
cards.notes: Go with friends to sample hands-on activities and entertainment; check the event page before heading over because programs can change.
cards.short_summary: A campus festival-style day with free public admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Stony Brook describes CommUniversity Day as a free, family-friendly festival-style event, and its registration page says admission is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Signature Programs and Events | University and Medicine Community Relations
cards.access_notes: Free and family-friendly; review the event page for the current program and any day-of details.

cards.title: Catch a SEA weekend event
cards.subtitle: Student Engagement & Activities
cards.notes: Use SB Engaged or CORQ to choose a Friday or Saturday program, then bring friends for the listed activity or performance.
cards.short_summary: Recurring free student programming on campus weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Stony Brook states that Student Engagement & Activities hosts free events every Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: For Stony Brook students; use SB Engaged or the CORQ app to confirm the current event, location, and participation details.

cards.title: Ride the Port Jeff shuttle
cards.subtitle: Between SBU and Port Jefferson Village
cards.notes: Bring a valid SBUID and ride with friends to Port Jefferson Village; use the service stops for a no-fare outing off campus.
cards.short_summary: A student-only, no-fare connection between campus and Port Jefferson.
cards.evidence_claim: Stony Brook calls the Port Jefferson/SBU shuttle a free-of-charge service for students with a valid SBUID.
cards.source_title: Welcome to SBU: Coming This Fall
cards.access_notes: Valid SBUID required. The page lists Friday and Saturday service and stops including the SAC loop and Port Jefferson Village Center.

cards.title: Attend an OSAC talk
cards.subtitle: Endeavour Hall, Room 120
cards.notes: Choose an OSAC speaker topic that interests your group, arrive a few minutes early, and compare takeaways after the talk.
cards.short_summary: A free public ocean-and-climate seminar series.
cards.evidence_claim: Stony Brook’s School of Marine and Atmospheric Sciences says all seminar talks are free and open to the public; OSAC meets Fridays in Endeavour Hall, Room 120.
cards.source_title: Outreach | School of Marine and Atmospheric Sciences
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public. OSAC is scheduled on Fridays; verify the semester speaker schedule before attending.

cards.entity_name: Topics in Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences Seminar
cards.title: Drop into a TAOS seminar
cards.subtitle: Endeavour Hall, Room 120
cards.notes: Make a midweek plan around a TAOS speaker, then use the topic as a prompt for a low-key science conversation afterward.
cards.short_summary: A Wednesday public seminar centered on atmospheric and oceanic science.
cards.evidence_claim: Stony Brook’s School of Marine and Atmospheric Sciences says all seminar talks are free and open to the public; TAOS meets Wednesdays in Endeavour Hall, Room 120.
cards.source_title: Outreach | School of Marine and Atmospheric Sciences
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public. TAOS is scheduled on Wednesdays; verify the semester speaker schedule before attending.

cards.title: Hear an economics seminar
cards.subtitle: Social & Behavioral Sciences Building, N603
cards.notes: Pick a speaker from the department schedule and attend with a classmate; save a question or discussion point for the walk back.
cards.short_summary: A public departmental speaker series in Social and Behavioral Sciences.
cards.evidence_claim: Stony Brook’s Department of Economics states that its seminars are free of charge and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free of charge and open to the public. The department lists seminars in Room N603; confirm the active semester schedule.

cards.title: Go to a library writers talk
cards.subtitle: Javits Room, Melville Library
cards.notes: Check the library’s event listing for a visiting author or faculty conversation, then meet in the Javits Room for the program.
cards.short_summary: Free author conversations hosted by University Libraries.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries describes its Writers Series as free lectures and conversations with Stony Brook faculty and visiting authors, held in the Javits Room and free and open to all.
cards.source_title: Events | Special Collections and University Archives
cards.access_notes: Free and open to all; consult the library events page for the next program and any registration information.

cards.title: Take the campus Art Crawl
cards.subtitle: Simons Center, Melville Library, Wang Center, and Staller Center
cards.notes: Follow the guided route with friends or join at one stop; gallery talks and the shared route make it easy to linger together.
cards.short_summary: A free guided tour linking several campus galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: Stony Brook reports that its Art Crawls unite campus galleries through free guided tours led by curators and are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Art Crawl Spotlights Amazing Work in Galleries Across Campus - SBU News
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public when scheduled. Check current gallery or University Libraries event listings for the next crawl route.
